reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Mondays in August have a specific texture. Summer is more than half over, the light is starting to slant differently in the evenings, and there's this quiet pressure to have made something of the season. When I was drinking, Mondays were for damage control — figuring out what I'd said, where my keys were, whether I still had a job. The week never really started. It just accumulated.

What nobody told me about sobriety is that Mondays become the point. Not the weekends. The Monday where you wake up on time, drink your coffee, actually hear what your coworker says instead of nodding through it. The Monday where you go for a run after work because you can. This is the life. Not the mountaintop, not the sober-anniversary post — the Tuesday morning that felt like a Tuesday morning, the grocery run where you weren't sweating out last night.

Durant's line about habit gets quoted to death, but it's true in a way that took me years to feel. You don't decide to be someone you can live with in one big move. You decide it in a hundred small ones, most of them boring. Show up for the ordinary Monday. That's where the actual life is being built.
reflection.meditation: Where in today, exactly as it is, can I show up more fully?

affirmations: I am building a life one ordinary day at a time, and today counts.
Today I get to be present for things I used to sleep through.
I have the capacity to handle this Monday without escaping it.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful today for the unremarkable stuff — a clear head at 7am, coffee I actually taste, a phone I'm not afraid to check. There was a version of me who couldn't imagine wanting a quiet Monday, let alone being grateful for one. That I get to be here, sober, on an ordinary August morning is not something I take lightly.
gratitude.closing: One day. This one. That's the whole assignment.
